claim: Hereditary gingival fibromatosis (HGF) is the most common genetic form of gingival fibromatosis which is featured as a localized or generalized overgrowth of gingivae.
source: Hereditary gingival fibromatosis (HGF) is the most common genetic form of gingival fibromatosis which is featured as a localized or generalized overgrowth of gingivae.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about HGF that draws from established medical knowledge and literature.

claim: Two genes (SOS1 and REST) have been identified as associated with HGF in a dominant inheritance pattern.
source: Currently two genes (SOS1 and REST), as well as four loci (2p22.1, 2p23.3–p22.3, 5q13–q22, and 11p15), have been identified as associated with HGF in a dominant inheritance pattern.
evidence: This statement references previously established findings in the literature about genetic associations with HGF.

claim: Four loci (2p22.1, 2p23.3–p22.3, 5q13–q22, and 11p15) have been identified as associated with HGF in a dominant inheritance pattern.
source: Currently two genes (SOS1 and REST), as well as four loci (2p22.1, 2p23.3–p22.3, 5q13–q22, and 11p15), have been identified as associated with HGF in a dominant inheritance pattern.
evidence: This statement references previously established findings in the literature about genetic loci associated with HGF.

claim: A novel heterozygous missense mutation (c.2812G > A) in zinc finger protein 862 gene (ZNF862) was identified in 13 individuals with autosomal-dominant HGF from a four-generation Chinese family.
source: Here, we report 13 individuals with autosomal-dominant HGF from a four-generation Chinese family. Whole-exome sequencing followed by further genetic co-segregation analysis was performed for the family members across three generations. A novel heterozygous missense mutation (c.2812G > A) in zinc finger protein 862 gene (ZNF862) was identified
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-exome sequencing data and genetic co-segregation analysis performed in the study.

claim: The c.2812G > A mutation in ZNF862 is absent among the population as per the Genome Aggregation Database.
source: A novel heterozygous missense mutation (c.2812G > A) in zinc finger protein 862 gene (ZNF862) was identified, and it is absent among the population as per the Genome Aggregation Database.
evidence: This claim is supported by database query results from the Genome Aggregation Database.

claim: ZNF862 increases profibrotic factors particularly COL1A1 synthesis resulting in HGF.
source: The functional study supports a biological role of ZNF862 for increasing the profibrotic factors particularly COL1A1 synthesis and hence resulting in HGF.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional studies including RNA sequencing and shRNA knockdown experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: This is the first identification of the physiological role of ZNF862 for the association with HGF.
source: Here, for the first time we identify the physiological role of ZNF862 for the association with the HGF.
evidence: This is a claim of novelty based on the authors' literature review and their own findings.

claim: GF could be complicated by epilepsy, hypertrichosis, and mental retardation.
source: GF could be complicated by epilepsy, hypertrichosis, and mental retardation (Balaji and Balaji, 2017; Snyder, 1965)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: GF can develop as a part of syndromes like Cowden's syndrome, Zimmerman-Laband syndrome, Cross syndrome, Rutherford syndrome, Ramon syndrome, Jones syndrome, Costello syndrome, Ectro-amelia syndrome, and hyaline fibromatosis syndrome.
source: or it can develop as a part of syndromes like Cowden's syndrome (Witkop, 1971), Zimmerman-Laband syndrome (Guglielmi et al., 2019), Cross syndrome (Poulopoulos et al., 2011), Rutherford syndrome (Häkkinen and Csiszar, 2007), Ramon syndrome (Suhanya et al., 2010), Jones syndrome (Gita et al., 2014), Costello syndrome (Hennekam, 2003), Ectro-amelia syndrome (Morey and Higgins, 1990), and hyaline fibromatosis syndrome (Hamada et al., 1980)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature describing these syndromes.

claim: GF may be caused by poor oral hygiene-related gingival inflammation, puberty, pregnancy, or a side effect of common medications such as calcium channel blockers (nifedipine and verapamil).
source: it may also be caused by poor oral hygiene-related gingival inflammation, puberty, pregnancy, or a side effect of the common medications such as calcium channel blockers (nifedipine and verapamil) (Livada and Shiloah, 2012)

claim: HGF is the most common genetic form of GF and usually transmitted as an autosomal-dominant inheritance pattern.
source: HGF is the most common genetic form of GF and usually transmitted as an autosomal-dominant inheritance pattern.

claim: Four loci (2p22.1 [MIM: 135,300], 5q13–q22 [MIM: 605,544], 2p23.3–p22.3 [MIM: 609,955], and 11p15 [MIM: 611,010]) have been identified associated with HGF.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Only three variants ATP7B (c.3403G > A), CDADC1 (c.83–13G > T), ZNF862 (c.2812G > A) were identified to be co-segregated with the phenotype among the 10 family members who underwent WES.

claim: Only ZNF862 (c.2812G > A) was validated to be co-segregated with the phenotype in all 23 alive members in this family.
